page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Curd from milk
steps.why: Lactobacillus ferments the lactose of milk to lactic acid, which sets the milk into curd — a daily food use of heterotrophic bacteria.
common_mistakes: Writing yeast for curd. Yeast is a fungus; curd formation is by bacteria (Lactobacillus).
steps.memory_tip: One food use and one medicine use: curd, then antibiotics.
steps.margin_note: Adding the name Lactobacillus makes the point exact.

steps.label: Antibiotics
lines: Many heterotrophic bacteria are used in

lines.text: Curd from milk; production of antibiotics.

steps.why: Antibiotic production is the medical use of heterotrophic bacteria; with curd it gives the two economically important uses asked for.
common_mistakes: Writing Penicillium here. Penicillium is a fungus; this question asks for bacterial uses.
Writing disease-causing as a use. Diseases are harm, not an economic use.
steps.memory_tip: Bacteria in food (curd) and bacteria in medicine (antibiotics).
steps.margin_note: Two one-line uses; nitrogen fixation in legume roots is an accepted alternative.

insider_note: Any two correct uses earn the marks — curd, antibiotics, or nitrogen fixation in legume roots — but a fungal example like Penicillium earns nothing here.
